critical_code_review_comments: ai_training_scheduler.py — clean separation: _run_batch (executor), _emit_alert (notification side-effect + log), _process_schedule (idempotent gate by last_run_date + hour/minute window), _worker_loop (60s tick). Good use of asyncio.Semaphore(3) for off-hours batch.
ai_training_scheduler.py — get_schedule returns sensible defaults (enabled=False, hour_utc=3, minute=0, alert_threshold=7.5) even when no DB doc exists. Avoids 404 noise on first UI load.
ai_training.py PUT /schedule — proper Pydantic-less manual validation with explicit 400 for hour/minute/threshold ranges. clean dict pattern + raise on empty payload prevents silent no-op.
ai_training.py — lazy import of services.ai_training_scheduler at bottom avoids circular import with routes/ai_training (good).
TrainingStudio.js ScheduleTab — Save uses optimistic UI with flash setTimeout(3000); error handling via alert() works but could be replaced with toast for consistency (low priority).

TrainingStudio.js — 'Próxima execução prevista' calc uses local Date but server uses UTC hours; display via toLocaleString is correct since input is hour_utc. Logic of bumping to next day when targetUtc<=now is sound.
Notification insert uses kind='training_drift' / severity='warning' — NotificationsBell should pick this up automatically (out of scope for this iter test).
(carryover from iter65) TrainingStudio.js is now ~1380 lines — recommend splitting into /TrainingStudio/{ScenariosTab,TestsTab,MatrixTab,HistoryTab,ScheduleTab}.js for maintainability.
action_items: (Optional/Low) Consider splitting TrainingStudio.js (~1380 lines) into per-tab modules.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Scheduler regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_iter66_ai_training_schedule.py (11 cases, ~3s). Worker is idempotent via last_run_date=YYYY-MM-DD; will NOT re-run today. To force a new auto-run for testing, manually clear last_run_date in ai_training_schedule collection OR call services.ai_training_scheduler.run_now(cid) which bypasses the date gate. The drift alert state (last_alert_at) is what drives the red banner — to test the 'no drift' UI variant, would need a batch with avg>=threshold. End-to-end is fully working.
